text: A bit per second, well then you have to wait. It takes time to do that. And then we have the MAC header. The MAC header again are, it's a non interesting bits from the point of view of the application. The size of the MAC header in WiFi may actually vary, depending on, for example, how many addresses you need. So if you are in a VSS isolated VSS as the one that you have got in your apartment, the only addresses that you need are the transmitter address and receiver address. If you are in an extended service set like your Monton G campus where we have many access points connected through, you know the the wired network. Then you may need four different addresses. And the reason for that is that in an extended service set you may have, as we know, access points that are connected to each other, right? We already explained the architecture of the network. And so if you are A and you want to send a packet to B, well then you have to send your packet to the access point you are connected with. This access point one will send the packet to access point two, and then access point two will deliver the packet to B. This happens in an extended service set.
